developments.label: PHP applicability needs SAPI and package evidence
developments.paraphrase: Both retained PHP records keep the four branch bounds and separately dated SAPI, request-state, distribution-backport and conditional CISA guidance. Neither a lower version number nor broad web-serving language establishes universal exploitability or an installed patch state.

qualified_context.label: Initial pair: upstream releases and backports
qualified_context.paraphrase: PHP identifies 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 for the initial pair. It also describes distribution/LTS fixes and minimal backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. A lower displayed vendor-package version can contain a backport; package evidence remains necessary.

qualified_context.label: Demonstration and other SAPIs
qualified_context.paraphrase: PHP describes an unauthenticated mod_php demonstration before application execution and qualifies susceptibility for other SAPIs. Broad web-serving risk does not establish identical demonstrated exploitability for every SAPI, deployment, release or patched package.

qualified_context.label: Request-state prerequisites
qualified_context.paraphrase: The separate advisory distinguishes demonstrations from candidate paths and configuration-dependent state shared by requests in one worker. No deployment prerequisites were verified for this edition.

qualified_context.label: Conditional CISA advice
qualified_context.paraphrase: CISA advises temporary offline status until patched or updated when an organization cannot update immediately or continues using unsupported PHP 8.1 or earlier. That condition does not prove every lower-numbered vendor build is unpatched. The retained evidence establishes a revision date, not initial publication time.

qualified_context.label: Separate follow-up path
qualified_context.paraphrase: For the later CVE-2026-115560, PHP described a next-regular-release plan and session.upload_progress.enabled=0 as an interim measure for the unusual path that switches php_binary or php_serialize to php with ini_set() before session_start(), while upload progress remains enabled. This does not completely mitigate the initial pair. A shipped third fix or historical registry absence is not established.
